historical_references.reference: Saint Otilia of Le Mans, also known as Otilia of Avenay or Otilia of the Forest, was a sixth-century Celtic hermitess and virgin martyr.
historical_references.context: Born in Brittany, Otilia led a secluded life in the forest near Le Mans. She was discovered by a hunter who was drawn to her by the light of a lantern that she used at night. After revealing her identity, Otilia was arrested by the local bishop and imprisoned. She was tortured but never wavered from her faith. Ultimately, she was executed by being thrown into a cauldron of boiling water, but her body was miraculously unharmed. She is now venerated as a saint and a patroness of students, virgins, and those seeking a hidden treasure.

historical_references.reference: Another Saint Otilia, also known as Otilia of Nursia, was an Italian Benedictine abbess and mystic of the sixth century.
historical_references.context: Born to a noble Roman family, Otilia was educated in the scriptures and later joined the Benedictine monastery of Monte Cassino. She became a renowned mystic and was later chosen by Pope Gregory the Great to establish a convent at Mons Amoena in the Sabine Mountains. Otilia's life was marked by numerous visions and ecstasies. She is now venerated as a patroness of the blind and those suffering from mental illness.
